slides.title: Everything you do is a do.
slides.text: Reading a list, ticking an item, searching your notes, syncing with a friend: each is a {do}, a small piece of JSON that says what to do. One engine runs them all.

slides.title: A simple query.
slides.text: “What's still open, soonest first?” A do takes data, narrows it and hands back an answer. It runs on your own device, over what you can already read.

slides.title: Changes are dos too.
slides.text: Ticking an item is a do. The engine checks your rule, turns it into CRDT ops, signs them and hands them to sync. A do is what you mean; ops are what gets stored.

slides.title: Walking a graph.
slides.text: Data links to data: a list to its items, an item to a photo, a person to their friends. A {walk} follows links hop by hop, and stops wherever your rules stop.

slides.title: Searching by words.
slides.text: A {search} finds the notes that best match your words, ranked the way search engines do it (BM25). The index is built on your device, from what you can read, and never leaves it.

slides.title: Searching by meaning.
slides.text: “Plumbing problems” should also find “water under the sink”. A {near} compares meaning as vectors and returns the closest entries. Same rule: the index is local.

slides.title: Dos chain together.
slides.text: The answer of one do is the input of the next. Search by meaning, follow the links to whoever is assigned, keep only what's open.

slides.title: New kinds of dos plug in.
slides.text: find, walk, search and near are {plugins}. Each one declares its name, the shape of its JSON, and what a rule must allow for it to run. A new plugin, say for maps or for time series, slots in the same way.

slides.title: Sync is dos too.
slides.text: Your device's sync plan is written as dos: what it wants, what it keeps, what it passes on. Here, your phone keeps three months of the house list and only fetches the photos you open.

slides.title: Rules name the dos.
slides.text: Before the engine runs a do, it looks up the rule behind it. A do runs only if the rule allows what it needs. No rule, no answer.

slides.title: Answers without reading.
slides.text: Some roles may ask a question but not read. One of your own devices runs it and returns only the answer: the street learns how many tasks are open, never which ones. Two safeguards: the rule fixes the exact question, so nobody can ask their way to the content, and only your own devices answer. This one is a promise kept by your devices, not by encryption.

slides.title: The engine, in short.
list: Every read, change, search and sync is a JSON do.
A change you do becomes CRDT ops that are signed and synced.
Dos chain: one do's answer feeds the next.
New kinds of dos plug in, each naming what a rule must allow.
Queries run where the keys are; others may get fixed answers, never the data.
